question: A benefits team proposes letting Claude decide which employee insurance claims are denied, with staff spot-checking only a sample each month. What is the greatest concern?
options: A) Claims processing is too repetitive a task for Claude, so the team would see no real time saving.
B) Insurance wording changes often, so the team would need to rewrite all of their prompts every single month.
C) A decision affecting people's benefits would be made with nobody accountable for each individual outcome.
D) Spot-checking a sample each month costs more staff time than reviewing every single claim would.
correct_answers: C) A decision affecting people's benefits would be made with nobody accountable for each individual outcome.
explanations: Repetitive, well-specified work is well suited to assistance; the problem is who owns the decision.
Keeping guidance current is routine maintenance, not the greatest risk in this proposal.
Correct. Decisions about entitlements need a person answerable for every case, not a sampled review afterwards.
Sampling is cheaper than full review; the concern is accountability, not cost.
